title: Baalbek trilithon stones
summary: Jay Anderson tells of Baalbek trilithon stones, about pre-Roman / 1st century at Baalbek, Lebanon, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: There's a series of stones called the trilithan stones, which are raised about 30 ft above the foundation blocks and placed with precision. They weigh conservative range 800 tons each, coming up to about 1,000 tons.

plain: Jay Anderson, who talks about ancient sites, describes on Jesse Michels's podcast the trilithon at Baalbek in Lebanon, a set of three huge stones. He says they sit about 30 feet above the foundation blocks, are placed with precision, and weigh at least 800 tons each, possibly close to 1,000 tons. The size and precision raise the question of who could have moved them, and how.
